2020 was the first major crash in my investment journey. And like everyone I freaked out as well. My portfolio was down 60%. But somehow I endured all and never stopped my SIP's and never took out any money. Then I saw the fruits of those in the consecutive years where my XIRR touched 15-16%.

You mentioned "Long-term wealth creation with with diversification and a reasonable balance between growth and risk." but the fund/category selection makes it look risky. Debt allocation is less than 25%. I would suggest reducing a few funds, also changing the SIP amount for funds if you want to reduce the amount of risk. I think you can remove the multi asset fund as you are already investing in all categories, also either remove the Value index fund or pick some value fund instead of index fund. I would recommend either adding a debt fund or Hybrid conservative fund or increasing the allocation to Balanced Advantage. As Gold fund investments are being stopped Gold ETF might have a premium over the gold price, you can stop the SIP in Gold ETF once that happens. Also for international funds i would keep the allocation lower as there is RBI limit due to which multiple international funds are not allowing SIP. The funds could be reduced but if you are not able to decide between categories you can start now and reduce categories as you move ahead. One option with a few less categories could be : Flexi cap, Mid cap, Small cap, Corp Debt, one international fund, gold and silver. With Indian Equity 60%, Debt 20%, International equity 10% and Gold+Silver 10%.
